ArXiv cs.AI.title: Don't Blame The Preferences: Examining The Emergence of Sycophancy in LLM Training
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.10045v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI sycophancy, the tendency of large language models (LLMs) to flatter users and affirm their beliefs, can undermine accuracy and contribute to misinformation, dependence, and overconfidence. Although prior work has benchmarked sycophancy in released models and proposed mitigations, its origins during training remain poorly understood. Preference alignment methods such as RLHF and DPO are often blamed, but their effects are rarely compared with earlier training stages. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Veterans' Mental Health Crisis Severity Annotation: Do LLMs Agree More Than Human Experts?
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.10048v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) offer a scalable approach for annotating mental health and crisis-related social media content, but their reliability in safety-critical tasks remains unclear. This study evaluates LLM-based crisis-severity annotation of veteran-related social media posts against annotations from eight Veteran Subject Matter Experts (SMEs). Using 149 tweets and five severity categories, we evaluate 15 open-source and 10 proprietary LLMs across eight prompt variants, examining annotation performance, inter-model agreement, prompt sens

ArXiv cs.AI.title: LoRazor: Trimming Adapter Execution for Efficient Multi-LoRA Serving
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.10049v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LoRA offers a parameter-efficient adaptation strategy, supporting multi-user workloads via customized adapters on a shared backbone. However, serving concurrent requests with different adapters introduces substantial computation and memory-management overhead. We ask the research question: Do all requests need their adapters throughout the whole generation process? Our motivational study reveals that employing LoRA adapters at every decoding step is unnecessary, releasing them early has limited impact on accuracy while substantially accelerating

ArXiv cs.AI.title: AYO: A Safe and Privacy-Preserving Platform for Studying Children's Interaction with LLMs
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.10054v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Children and adolescents are increasingly interacting with generative AI and large language models (LLMs), yet little is known about how these interactions may influence their development, beliefs, and behavior. Existing research has relied heavily on surveys, while direct study of children's interactions with LLMs presents substantial challenges related to safety, privacy, consent, and experimental control. We introduce AYO (AI Youth Open Science), an open-source platform designed for safe and systematic research on children's interactions with

ArXiv cs.AI.title: META-IR: Meta-Introspective Reasoning for Adaptive Safety Alignment in LLM
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.10089v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks and harmful-content prompts, particularly under adversarial distribution shifts where static alignment pipelines fail to generalize. Although introspective methods such as STAIR strengthen refusal consistency, they depend on fixed self-evaluation policies that cannot rapidly adapt to evolving manipulation strategies. To overcome these limitations, this paper introduces META-IR, a meta-introspective reasoning framework that enhances safety alignment through meta-learning-driven a

ArXiv cs.AI.title: The Infrastructure Divide: Analyzing Community Stance on Data Center Development via Reddit
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.10109v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The rapid expansion of AI-driven data center construction has outpaced public engagement: an estimated $64 billion in U.S. data center projects were blocked or delayed by local opposition between May 2024 and March 2025, yet the concerns driving this resistance remain poorly characterized. Prior engagement methods such as surveys and hearings are introduced late in the planning process, and no study has systematically mined social media to measure community stance at scale. To address this gap, this study presents an LLM-powered opinion-mining f

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Homeopathic Learning: Diluting poisoned fine-tuning data can strengthen its effect
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.10110v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study homeopathic learning, a phenomenon where poisoned training data with little effect on its own can create a hidden backdoor once clean, contrasting data is added. In our experiments, a model fine-tuned only on a "poison" dataset associated with a trait T (such as speaking German or being misaligned) does not learn T. Surprisingly, adding similarly formatted "clean" data not associated with T causes the model to learn T. This effect requires that the poison data have an identifying "trigger" feature that is absent from the clean data. We

ArXiv cs.AI.title: What Is the Value of AI-Involved Art? Evidence From a Juried In-Person Exhibition
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.10150v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: What is the value of AI-involved art, and to whom does it belong? We begin to answer these questions using data from an in-person, juried AI art exhibition. Our study involved artists, lawyers, and computer scientists (N=209) as either creators or evaluators of AI-involved artworks. We found that nearly half of evaluators reported willingness to buy an artwork, with pricing correlating with perceived artistic value---creativity and visual appeal---as well as the effort necessary to create it. ArXiv cs.AI.title: WorldMind: Test-Time Scaling for Visual Spatial Reasoning through Latent World Simulation
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.10151v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have continuous deficiency in spatial reasoning tasks that require \emph{mental spatial transformation}, such as reasoning under hypothetical changes in viewpoint or position, known as perspective-taking tasks. Existing approaches either scale linguistic reasoning or augment VLMs with static geometric representations, but neither directly enables active transformation of the represented scene. ArXiv cs.AI.title: DeepResearch RewardBench: Evaluating Reward Models for Deep Research Report
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.10156v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Empowered by Large Language Models (LLMs), deep research systems integrate online information into research reports through multi-step web searching and information synthesis. Evaluating these reports presents a significant challenge due to their long context, high information density, and domain specificity, necessitating the use of AI evaluation as a substitute for prohibitively expensive human assessment. However, few studies have examined the effectiveness of existing reward models or LLMs in understanding and evaluating such research report

ArXiv cs.AI.title: AutoEMatic: Runtime-Adaptive Mixed-Precision LLM Inference via Automatic Exponent-Mantissa Refinement
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.10165v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Existing LLM post-training quantization techniques determine precision before inference begins, yet the precision a model requires varies dynamically across prompts, layers, and inference phases. We present AutoEMatic, a full-stack co-design that adapts the precision of weights, activations, and the KV cache at runtime. A lightweight policy selects each layer's precision at every prefill and decode step from two runtime signals: the entropy of the next-token distribution and the magnitude of each layer's update to its hidden states. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Key Institutional Considerations for Designing Effective Independent Verification Organizations
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.10168v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Independent verification organizations (IVOs) have emerged as a popular, bipartisan solution for facilitating high-quality independent evaluations of AI technologies. But momentum is outpacing design: there is emerging consensus on the necessary operating conditions for robust IVOs, but little discourse on institutional and policy specifications to ensure those conditions are met. ArXiv cs.AI.title: AVCORP: Identifying and Resisting Deception via Communication Theory and Theory of Mind
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.10176v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Today's LLM-based agents are vulnerable to deception by users and other agents. Defending against deception requires Theory of Mind (ToM) reasoning to infer the beliefs and goals of others as well as modeling tactics based on communication theory. To enable training models to detect deception, we adopt the well-known deception game, Avalon. We present a corpus, AVCORP, of 5,000 annotated utterances from 250 games of Avalon. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Generative Active Learning for Label-Efficient Pan-Organ Ultrasound Diagnosis
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.10180v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Medical ultrasound (US) enables real-time, non-invasive diagnosis, yet building US-based AI systems is limited by data scarcity, costly expert annotation, and limited cross-center generalizability. Privacy constraints and instance-level reporting hinder the collection of diverse abnormal cases and frame-level labels, while repeated retraining for new centers increases computational cost. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Ensemble Routing for Prompt-Adaptive Cost-Aware LLM Inference
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.10193v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly support Web-based services that must balance response quality and inference cost across heterogeneous requests. Conventional routing selects one model per prompt, while fixed ensembles cannot adapt their composition and cost to individual requests. We introduce PISA, a prompt-adaptive, cost-aware single-model router, and PISA-E, its extension to ensemble routing. At the core of both methods, PISA combines soft cluster memberships with model-specific predictors to estimate individual model capabilities. B

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Process then Retrieve: Investigating the Origins of the Modality Gap in Vision-Language Models
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.09897v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Understanding the origins of the modality gap in vision language models remains a significant challenge. This work investigates whether differences in information density between modality specific tokens at the embedding layer contribute to this imbalance. We show that text tokens enter the model with much lower semantic density than visual tokens, driving early layers to focus on processing text representations before combining them with vision. Through mechanistic analysis, we demonstrate that replacing vision token positions with their semant

ArXiv cs.LG.title: MAGE: Towards Generalizable Multi-timescale EEG Representations
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.09928v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) data plays an important role in understanding human brain activity, with various major applications. While current approaches, which largely build on EEG foundation models, have demonstrated strong performance across datasets and tasks, they typically rely on a fixed temporal scale. This design choice limits their ability to capture characteristics of neural dynamic behavior, often spanning across multiple timescales, which are naturally captured in EEG recordings. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Causal Discovery Bench: Can LLMs Autonomously Conduct Effective Experiments?
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.09934v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As large language model (LLM) agents get actively adopted for autonomous research, they must not only reason over existing evidence, but also design informative experiments, allocate resources, analyze sequential observations, and decide when to stop and make conclusions. Yet these capabilities remain poorly measured. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.09935v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Resource-constrained IoT devices cache learned models for real-time decisions, but frequent updates incur substantial bandwidth, energy, and service overhead. Because decision-relevant model differences need not grow with elapsed time, we define Age of Intelligence (AoInt) as a model-version-relative, client-specific, and action utility distortion, and formulate synchronization as a tradeoff between stale-decision regret and refresh cost. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.10046v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper describes the 2026 edition of the Topological Deep Learning Challenge: Bridging the Gap, hosted at the second Topology, Algebra, and Geometry in Data Science (TAG-DS) Conference. Where previous editions grew the modelling and data ecosystem of Topological Deep Learning (TDL), this edition set out to place Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Topological Neural Networks (TNNs) side by side under a single evaluation pipeline. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Selected-Risk Calibration for Feasibility at Returned Decisions
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.10050v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: When an optimization problem uses a surrogate constraint, a decision that is feasible for the surrogate need not be feasible for the true constraint. We propose Selected-Risk Calibration (SRC), a framework that calibrates a learned constraint against the optimizer's returned decisions for objectives drawn from a given distribution. SRC guarantees that, with probability at least $1-\delta$, every margin it certifies on held-out objectives has selected risk, the probability that the returned decision is infeasible, of at most $\gamma$. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.10051v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Operator learning seeks to approximate function-to-function maps in a way that remains stable when the input discretization changes, a property sometimes called "discretization invariance". We consider a quantitative refinement of this idea, called $\textit{uniform discretization stability}$, which builds on a common representation of input functions and their discretizations as probability measures and provides a H\"older bound relating output changes to the Wasserstein distance between these measures. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.10082v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) is a promising modality for brain-computer interfaces and cognitive state decoding, but progress in machine learning for fNIRS has been limited by small, isolated datasets and inconsistent evaluation protocols. We introduce fNIRSAtlas, the largest open benchmark for fNIRS classification to date, comprising 23 classification tasks from 19 public data collections, spanning diverse experimental paradigms, including motor execution, motor imagery, mental arithmetic, working memory, and emotion recognitio

ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.10086v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sheet metal components often consist of a global geometry, such as the corner radii and forming depth of a corner component, and local features added to it. During forming, both affect material flow. A surrogate learning all their combinations may need large training data. However, the same local feature type is often used on many global geometries. This study therefore partly decouples local features from the global geometry. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Coordinated Mixed-Precision KV Cache Quantization for Efficient LLM-based Multi-agent Systems
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.10096v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM-based multi-agent systems solve complex tasks through collaboration, but their growing, simultaneously resident key-value (KV) caches create a memory bottleneck. Applying single-model quantization policies independently ignores differences in agents' precision needs, potentially degrading collective reasoning. We introduce Coordinated Mixed-Precision KV Cache Quantization (CoMixKV), which combines online sensitivity estimation with joint agent-layer bit-width allocation under a shared memory budget. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.10145v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Clinical trial screening requires assessing large numbers of patient-trial pairs to prioritize candidates for detailed eligibility review, often under restrictions on sharing patient records. We introduce TrialJev, an open-weight eligibility scorer that uses LoRA-adapted Qwen models and a pointer head to score natural-language answer options in a single forward pass, without autoregressive decoding. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.10153v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In clinical applications, patients undergo different combinations of tests, and machine learning models must therefore ensure accurate predictions across heterogeneous feature spaces. Current approaches upweight the patients with the highest loss, without accounting for the limited predictive information in their features preventing their loss from going any lower. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.10186v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Neural additive models (NAMs) offer interpretability but lack expressivity due to their rigid additive structure, whereas multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) achieve universal approximation at the cost of transparency. We establish the first theoretical foundation for projected neural additive models (PNAMs), which augment NAMs with a learnable linear transformation $\boldsymbol{T}$ to capture cross-variable interactions. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Fast Accurate Quantum Monte Carlo without Metropolis Adjustment
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.10187v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In quantum systems, physical quantities of interest can be expressed as expectation values of a probability distribution, which allows their estimation by Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods. This approach, an instance of Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC), plays a central role in obtaining predictions of system properties relevant to condensed matter and high energy physics. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.10188v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Stochastic bilevel optimization provides a general framework for many machine learning applications, such as hyperparameter learning, data reweighting, language model alignment, and actor-critic reinforcement learning.
